title: Monitor a log file for new lines
description: Follow a log file you are authorized to monitor and print appended lines.
code:
from pathlib import Path
import time
log = Path("app.log")
print("Waiting for new log entries...")
with log.open("r", errors="replace") as handle:
    handle.seek(0, 2)
    while True:
        line = handle.readline()
        if line:
            print(line, end="")
        else:
            time.sleep(1)

title: Alert on repeated failed logins in a sample file
description: Count repeated authentication failures in an authorized log excerpt.
code:
from pathlib import Path
from collections import Counter
import re
text = Path("auth.log").read_text(errors="replace")
counts = Counter(re.findall(r"failed login for user=([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)", text, re.I))
for account, total in counts.items():
    if total >= 5:
        print(f"REVIEW: {account} has {total} failed login events")

title: Write JSON Lines security events
description: Append structured events to a local JSONL file for later analysis.
code:
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
event = {
    "time": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
    "event": "permission_check",
    "target": "cyber-lab",
    "status": "reviewed"
}
with open("security-events.jsonl", "a", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    file.write(json.dumps(event) + "\n")
print("Event appended")

title: Create a simple security summary report
description: Build a short text report from findings collected during your own lab checks.
code:
from datetime import datetime, timezone
findings = [
    {"name": "Missing security header", "severity": "Medium"},
    {"name": "Debug mode enabled", "severity": "High"},
]
lines = [
    "CYBER LAB PRO — SECURITY SUMMARY",
    f"Generated: {datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()}",
    f"Total findings: {len(findings)}",
]
for item in findings:
    lines.append(f"- {item['severity']}: {item['name']}")
open("security-summary.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(lines))
print("Report saved: security-summary.txt")

title: Export findings to CSV
description: Save lab findings in CSV format for tracking and review.
code:
import csv
findings = [
    {"id": "CLP-001", "title": "Missing CSP", "severity": "Medium", "status": "Open"},
    {"id": "CLP-002", "title": "Weak access control", "severity": "High", "status": "Fixed"},
]
with open("findings.csv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    writer = csv.DictWriter(file, fieldnames=["id", "title", "severity", "status"])
    writer.writeheader()
    writer.writerows(findings)
print("CSV report created")

title: Calculate a simple risk priority score
description: Use an illustrative likelihood × impact score; this is not a formal CVSS calculation.
code:
def risk_score(likelihood, impact):
    if not (1 <= likelihood <= 5 and 1 <= impact <= 5):
        raise ValueError("Scores must be from 1 to 5")
    return likelihood * impact

score = risk_score(4, 5)
print("Risk score:", score)
print("Priority:", "High" if score >= 15 else "Review")

title: Check a local TCP port safely
description: Test one explicitly chosen loopback port on your own device.
code:
import socket
host, port = "127.0.0.1", 8000
with socket.socket() as sock:
    sock.settimeout(2)
    result = sock.connect_ex((host, port))
print("OPEN" if result == 0 else "CLOSED or unavailable")
